normative_extracts.quote: A stream is an independent, bidirectional sequence of frames exchanged between the client and server within an HTTP/2 connection.
HTTP/3 uses QUIC streams, preventing a lost packet on one stream from blocking delivery of data on other streams.

engine_internals.mechanism_summary: Interleaves binary frames from concurrent requests over a single connection; HTTP/3 moves multiplexing from TCP to QUIC to isolate packet loss per stream.

production_failures.symptom: High-packet-loss mobile users stall on all assets simultaneously despite HTTP/2
production_failures.root_cause: HTTP/2 multiplexes streams over a single TCP connection; one dropped TCP segment halts the entire kernel receive buffer (TCP head-of-line blocking).
production_failures.mitigation: Enable HTTP/3 (QUIC) on the CDN/edge and verify Alt-Svc headers are advertised.

production_failures.symptom: Domain sharding degrades Time to First Byte under HTTP/2
production_failures.root_cause: Splitting assets across multiple hostnames forces redundant TLS handshakes and prevents HPACK header compression and prioritization across streams.
production_failures.mitigation: Consolidate static assets onto a single origin or coalesced certificate SAN so the browser reuses one multiplexed connection.
